To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have performed laser spectroscopy on the neutron deficient gold nuclei and determined the magnetic moment, quadrupole moment and change in charge radius.
the nuclear magnetic moments of the odd A gold isotopic chain 185 195Au are well reproduced by the particle triaxial-rotor model calculation.
The spectroscopic quadrupolar moments of 191,195,197Au were measured for the first time by collinear laser-spectroscopy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electromagnetic moments and nuclear shapes, in particular with quadrupole and hexadecaple deformation of neutron deficient gold nuclei.
the study of electromagnetic properties of the neutron deficient isotopes of the element Gold.
the study of the evolution of nuclear shapes and electromagnetic moments in odd A gold isotopic chain and the comparison with a particle triaxile rotor model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the odd A and odd A gold isotopic chains are prolate, triaxial and oblate shaped, respectively.
the odd A gold isotopic chain is triaxially deformed in the region of N =104, while the even A isotopes are oblate in the region of the closed neutron shell at N =102.
the nuclear shapes of gold isotopes are very sensitive to changes in neutron number.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ground states of 183Au, 185Au and 187,189,191Au are triaxial with the same deformation parameters, while 186,190Au have oblate ground states and 188Au is prolate.
a triaxial rotor particle model calculation with a fixed deformation parameter (4 0) is in good agreement with the experimental data for the odd A and oddodd gold isotopes.
the particle triaxial model is able to describe the nuclear ground states of gold isotopes in the region of N = 104, 105, and 106 in a consistent way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the nuclear shape of gold isotopes is more complex than the traditional picture of a smooth evolution from prolate to triaxial shapes in the region of neutron numbers N=106, 107, 108, as predicted by the shell model.
, the particle triaxial model is able to describe the electromagnetic moments and deformation properties of neutron deficient gold nuclei very well.
the particle triaxial model is able to describe very well all available experimental data for odd A and odd-odd gold isotopes.
